feasibility.verdict: Partially feasible: single-column ELM can simulate snowmelt-onset day-of-year at each SNOTEL location and elevation dependence can be diagnosed across columns, but the *atmospheric* lapse rate itself is a prescribed forcing input, not an emergent ELM output, so the 'local lapse rate' must be imposed (via elevation-adjusted DATM) rather than dynamically resolved.
answerable: Day-of-year of snowmelt onset at each individual SNOTEL column location
Ranking/spread of melt-onset DOY across the elevation gradient
Sensitivity of melt-onset DOY to the imposed near-surface temperature lapse rate (dDOY/dElevation) between stations on the same ridge
SWE peak timing and ablation duration per column
not_answerable: The true observed atmospheric lapse rate between stations (ELM ingests, not derives, the temperature-elevation relationship)
Sub-grid lateral snow redistribution / wind-drift between adjacent stations (not represented in single-column mode)
Validation against actual SNOTEL SWE observations without supplying that observed data as an external comparison dataset

parsed.n_justification: Four Naches-basin SNOTEL sites are chosen: two pairs that lie on common ridge alignments spanning distinct elevation bands. This gives at least two low/high elevation contrasts on the same ridge so a local temperature lapse rate (dT/dz) and its imprint on melt-onset DOY (dDOY/dz) can be regressed, while keeping the campaign small and runnable.
requires_capabilities: Single-column ELM (ELM-SCM) point runs at each SNOTEL lat/lon
Elevation-adjusted DATM forcing (per-column temperature/pressure downscaling using an imposed lapse rate) to represent inter-station elevation differences
Daily-resolution history output to detect melt-onset DOY (first sustained decline in H2OSNO / positive QFLX_SNOMELT)
Spin-up capability for soil/snow state initialization
Post-processing regression of melt-onset DOY vs. station elevation
assumptions: SNOTEL station coordinates and elevations approximated from published NRCS metadata for the Naches/upper-Yakima basin (Bumping Lake ~1036 m, Morse Lake ~1661 m, White Pass ~1372 m, Pigtail Peak ~1798 m).

GSWP3/CLMNCEP-style reanalysis forcing is downscaled to each column elevation using a specified environmental lapse rate (default ~6.5 K/km), which is treated as the tunable 'imposed local lapse rate' for sensitivity tests.
Melt-onset DOY defined as the first day-of-year with a sustained (>=3 consecutive days) decrease in SWE (H2OSNO) after the seasonal peak.
First water year (2000-10-01 to 2001-09-30) treated as spin-up; analysis uses 2001-2020 water years.
Soil textures assigned as coarse mountain-soil approximations pending site-specific pedon data.
Single-column mode omits lateral/wind snow redistribution; results reflect vertical energy-balance controls only.
